neighbours.label: verbs of reaching out to someone with a request or inquiry ('wrote asking', 'to ask', 'contacts you'); messages that only thank or inform stay lower
fire: A stranger emailed me on Monday asking if I still sold the bike.
Several parents wrote to the principal to ask about the new schedule.
My landlord texted me last night asking when I could pay the rent.
If a caller contacts you about your account, hang up.
The editor phoned the author twice asking for the final chapter.
Hundreds of fans wrote to the studio to ask for a sequel.
An old classmate messaged me yesterday asking whether I was in town.
The charity sent letters to residents asking for small donations.
quiet: A stranger emailed me on Monday with a photo of the bike.
Several parents wrote to the principal to thank her for the new schedule.
My landlord texted me last night with a photo of the new door.
If a caller is rude to you on the phone, hang up.
The editor phoned the author twice to praise the final chapter.
Hundreds of fans wrote to the studio to celebrate the anniversary.
An old classmate messaged me yesterday with a happy birthday note.
The charity sent letters to residents with its yearly report.

predictions: fire 0.35-1.0 on ask/asking/contact after a message or call; thank/about frames below 0.2
notes: Card: ' asking' x4, ' ask' x4, ' asked' x3, ' contacts', 'обращаться'. Probe: 'called me last week asking whether' 0.992, 'wrote to the mayor to ask for' 0.393, 'bank contacts you' 0.339; 'to thank him' 0.127, 'about the new playground' 0.126; but 'telling me about' leaked 0.473 and 'beat the dust out' 0.352, so informing verbs are avoided in near misses.
